The employee initials are now always circles. I haven't looked at it in the running app yet; reload the page to see the change. The new test and the existing team tests pass, and lint is clean.

**Cause:** the code already asked for a circle, but it was being ignored. `tile(..., round_=True)` set `borderRadius: 50%` through Reflex's `style` prop. Reflex turns that into a generated CSS class, and the shared `.aq-tile { border-radius: 7px }` rule beat that class, so the avatar came out as a rounded square.

**Fix** in [list_view.py](components/alloq-commons/src/alloq_commons/components/list_view.py):
- Round tiles now get a `data-shape="round"` attribute instead of the inline style.
- A new rule, `.aq-tile[data-shape=round] { border-radius: 50% }`, sits after the large-size rule, so it also wins for the big avatar in the inspector.

This fixes every place that uses the round tile: the team list, the employee inspector and the team members in the project inspector. I added a test for it in [test_list_view.py](components/alloq-commons/tests/test_list_view.py).

    value = 5381

content.text:
Employee avatars now take their color from the employee's primary role (the "key role") on every screen. Everyone with the same primary role gets the same color, and each role gets its own. All tests, lint and type checks pass. I couldn't look at it in the app because another session has the browser open, so please reload a page to see it. Nothing is committed.

**How the color is picked**
- A new function, `role_avatar_color` in [role_colors.py](components/alloq-commons/src/alloq_commons/role_colors.py), turns the role's ID into a strong color with white initials.
- Each next role ID gets a color far from the ones before it, so roles with nearby IDs never look alike. The test checks that the first 20 role IDs all get different colors. With many more roles than that, two of them could end up looking very similar.
- People without a primary role get a neutral gray.
- The `Employee` model now has an `avatar_color` field, filled in the same way as `workload_percent`. All screens read the color from there, so it is defined in one place.

**Screens changed**

| Screen | Before |
|---|---|
| Team list and employee inspector | Color picked by employee ID from a list of 6 colors |
| Employee card | Accent color for everyone |
| Project card team avatars and project inspector team list | Accent color or gray for everyone |
| Absence planner (rows and upcoming absences) | Mantine's color picked from the person's name |
| Plan project dialog (employee list and preview) | Accent color for everyone |

All of these now use the same filled style, so a person looks the same everywhere.

**Two things to know**
- The colored role badges still get their pale colors from the role name, so a badge and its avatar won't always be the same hue. I can switch the badges to the role ID too if you want them to match.
- [shell.py](components/alloq-commons/src/alloq_commons/components/shell.py) was changed while I worked (a `SegmentedControl` padding rule). That wasn't me, so I left it as it is.
